methodological_rigor.justification: This TCGA-based bioinformatics study identifies 10 ferroptosis-related genes (FRGs) via LASSO Cox regression in 415 HPV-negative HNSCC patients, with in vitro validation of TRIB3 in CAL27 (HPV-negative) and UPCI-SCC-090 (HPV-positive) cells using siRNA knockdown and overexpression with ferroptosis markers (Fe2+, GSH, MDA, ROS, TEM). IHC validation of TRIB3 in 179 clinical samples adds histopathological support. The use of training/testing/combined cohort split for model validation and time-dependent ROC curves adds rigor. Key limitations include reliance on TCGA retrospective data, in vitro validation limited to single cell lines per HPV group, no prospective cohort validation, and the mechanistic pathway by which TRIB3 regulates ferroptosis remains uncharacterized.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective bioinformatics plus in vitro validation study mapping to Oxford LoE 4. HPV-negative HNSCC has a distinct biology and worse prognosis than HPV-positive disease, and ferroptosis-based prognostic stratification is an active area. The 10-FRG risk score with AUC >0.7 at most time points represents potentially useful prognostic modeling. However, all data are retrospective, and clinical implementation requires prospective multicenter validation.

reporting_quality.justification: TCGA data access, bioinformatics packages (R versions, ConsensusClusterPlus, CIBERSORT), statistical thresholds, and IHC protocols are described. The ferroptosis database source is cited. TRIB3 siRNA sequences and cell line authentication are reported. However, no formal reporting checklist (REMARK, TRIPOD) is applied despite the prognostic biomarker/model development nature of the study, and PROSPERO registration is absent. TCGA data are publicly accessible but extracted data for the prognostic model are not separately deposited.

novelty_literature.justification: While ferroptosis gene signatures in HNSCC have been published (cited refs 31, 32), the HPV-stratification strategy — identifying FRG differences specifically between HPV-negative and HPV-positive HNSCC — is a meaningful methodological advance. The identification of TRIB3 as a ferroptosis regulator in HPV-negative HNSCC with IHC validation in 179 clinical samples and functional in vitro confirmation is incrementally novel. AGPAT3 as a novel FRG not previously linked to ferroptosis is a specific new finding.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript follows a logical structure from bioinformatics discovery through clinical validation to in vitro functional characterization. The LASSO model development and nomogram construction are clearly explained. The discussion appropriately contextualizes the 10 FRGs with existing literature on EGFR, ACSL1, PPARG, and BNIP3 in ferroptosis. Some sections of the bioinformatics results (CIBERSORT immune infiltration) are descriptive without clear mechanistic integration into the TRIB3 narrative. Limitations are explicitly listed, which reflects appropriate scientific transparency.

key_strengths: HPV-stratified ferroptosis analysis fills a specific biological gap, recognizing that HPV-positive and HPV-negative HNSCC have distinct oncogenic drivers
IHC validation of TRIB3 in 179 clinical HNSCC specimens provides histopathological support beyond in silico analysis
Bidirectional TRIB3 functional validation (knockdown in HPV-negative, overexpression in HPV-positive) with consistent ferroptosis marker changes strengthens mechanistic claims
key_concerns: TRIB3 functional validation limited to single cell lines per HPV subtype; results require confirmation in additional HPV-negative lines (SCC-25, HN6) as acknowledged by authors
No in vivo validation; the prognostic model requires prospective multicenter validation before clinical utility can be assessed
TRIPOD/REMARK reporting guidelines not applied despite this being a prognostic biomarker model development study; PROSPERO pre-registration absent
chief_reviewer.rationale: A reasonably executed bioinformatics-plus-functional study identifying TRIB3 as a ferroptosis regulator in HPV-negative HNSCC with a 10-FRG prognostic signature. The HPV stratification approach and dual-direction TRIB3 validation support Tier 3 publication after minor revisions expanding in vitro validation to additional cell lines.
